coaching.headline: Three-stack wins 22 to 16 with four of five lanes unfavored on paper: the fights decided it, not the draft sheet.
coaching.team: The support matchup against Adele read favored the entire game, and the offlane against Scarlett, down early, evened out by the late game. On paper four of the five lanes were unfavored, jungle, midlane, offlane and carry all read as the enemy's for some or all of the game, and the start reflected it: a bad trade in the river and a lost fight at the enemy's own Fangtooth conceded the game's first major inside the first eight minutes. From there the team started winning the fights that mattered, eight of the next nine skirmishes, the biggest a five-for-zero wipe at the squad's own Fangtooth that the enemy never recovered from. River and jungle-seedling control tilted the team's way for the rest of the game, and towers followed, 7 to 5, alongside a 70,056 to 17,601 objective-damage split. The one gap in an otherwise dominant map presence: Orb Prime at 27 minutes went to the enemy with the whole squad alive and nobody near it, in the same stretch a 24-minute fight at the team's own outer tower was lost 0-2 while the ahead-in-lane support could have rotated in to flip the numbers. The Primal Fangtooth pickup at 28 minutes was converted immediately into an inhibitor, and the game closed out from there. Next game: keep a body watching the enemy's own jungle timers even mid win streak, and send the ahead-in-lane player into a fight rather than let it go 0-2.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The bad trade in the river and the loss of the game's first Fangtooth by the eight-minute mark put the team in an early hole against four unfavored matchups on paper. The turn was the run from the 10.8-minute skirmish through the 21.9-minute tower fight, eight wins in nine tries, capped by a 5-for-0 wipe at the squad's own Fangtooth that the enemy never recovered from.
coaching.whatWorked: The clearest strength was converting won fights into map progress: the squad cashed seven of its eleven won fights into a tower or objective within 90 seconds, more than double the two conversions the opponents managed from three wins, which is why a 22-to-16 edge in majors turned into a 7-to-5 tower lead and 70,056 to 17,601 in objective damage.

perPlayer.219ccde6-c9e2-4a6e-900c-65304c72c960: Yin's jungle matchup against Bayle read as the enemy's the entire game, and it showed early: Bayle caught Yin three times across the game, and two of those deaths, at 7.1 and 24.3 minutes, directly preceded the enemy taking the game's first Fangtooth and an outer tower. Yin still finished 8 kills and 7 assists and led the team in damage to objectives with 32,850. The one flag worth carrying forward is that none of Yin's four items carried armor against a lineup that was four-fifths physical.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Phase's matchup against Adele was the one lane that read favored the entire game, and 28 assists plus 12 wards, the most on the squad, reflect a support who was in the right place from minute one. All three of Phase's deaths came in the first 12 minutes, two of them directly preceding the enemy majors that followed, but there were zero more deaths across the remaining 21 minutes while the assists kept climbing. The Adele matchup reading favored the whole game is what made this support lane work.
perPlayer.29199160-1218-49ea-9f15-0717d1726afb: Legion's matchup against Kira read as the enemy's the whole game on paper, but the result said otherwise: 15 kills against 2 deaths and a team-high 37,515 damage to heroes made Legion the most productive player on either team. Both deaths came late, at 20.0 and 29.2 minutes, in team fights rather than in the lane itself. Skipping the meta core's Malady and Deathstalker for anti-heal and a late defensive item traded some armor shred for the survivability that kept Legion converting kills instead of trading them.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Shinbi's matchup against Scarlett went the enemy's way early before evening out, and Shinbi closed the game with zero deaths across 33 minutes and 33,949 damage to heroes, second-highest on the team. The offlane recovering from behind to even by the late game is the signal that matters here. None of Shinbi's five items carried armor either, though it never cost anything here, with Bayle the one repeatedly getting picked off rather than landing a dive.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Renna's matchup against Howitzer read as the enemy's for the entire game, but the box score says otherwise: 10 kills, 11 assists and 28,977 damage to heroes on a fully completed core. Renna's two deaths came in the opening river bad trade at 3.7 minutes, and in the 24-minute fight at the squad's own outer tower that was lost 0-2. Neither was a lane problem: the first was a fight the team shouldn't have started, and the second could have gone differently with a rotation from the support player who was alive and ahead in lane.

14.5.call: Grouping in front of our own Fangtooth for the full engage was the right read: with almost no hard crowd control on this side, forcing the fight on top of an objective the whole enemy team already committed to is how this comp wins a coin-toss 5v5, and the 5-for-0 result took the buff outright.

27.1.call: The 3-for-0 fight at their inner tower was clean, but it landed at the exact moment Orb Prime went to the enemy with the whole squad alive and nobody near it. The squad committed five to the fight at their inner tower and won it, but that let the enemy take Orb Prime uncontested elsewhere on the map at the same time — the fight was won, but the objective was traded away for it.

28.9.call: Following the Primal Fangtooth pickup straight into the 4-2 fight at the inner tower was the correct way to spend the buff, and the inhibitor that fell right after is the direct payoff of using it immediately instead of letting it sit.

219ccde6-c9e2-4a6e-900c-65304c72c960.build: Yin's finished build, Manta Scythe, Onixian Quiver, Terminus and Imperator, is a crit-and-lifesteal package built around Onixian Quiver's extra projectiles and Terminus's overheal shield, which is what let Yin keep re-engaging fights rather than trade once and back off. The winning core's other two items, Sky Splitter and Lightning Hawk, were skipped; Sky Splitter in particular hits for a cut of the target's current health on repeated attacks, which chews through a stacked-up frontline faster than crit damage alone. None of the four items carried armor either, against a lineup that was four-fifths physical with Kira alone putting up 25,672 damage to heroes, and Bayle caught Yin three times before that gap in sustain closed.
219ccde6-c9e2-4a6e-900c-65304c72c960.eternal: The engine's recommended loadout for Yin runs the Vermis major with the Serration and Melting Point minors, an on-hit package that rewards landing repeated basic attacks on the same target and hits harder the tankier that target is, a good match for a duelist whose plan is to isolate one enemy and grind them down rather than land a single big combo. That is a real trade against a burst-focused major: Yin gives up a big first-hit spike for damage that compounds the longer a one-on-one runs, which lines up with how the jungle matchup actually played out, repeated extended skirmishes with Bayle rather than one clean pick.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Phase finished the entire winning core, Marshal, Enra's Blessing and Galaxy Greaves, then added Windcaller and Vanguardian on top, both defensive items that stack armor, with Vanguardian also granting a team-wide armor and tenacity aura. Against a lineup that was four-fifths physical and carried two knockback abilities, Howitzer's Land Mine and Bayle's Kingslayer, that extra armor is exactly what the rest of the squad was missing, since Yin and Shinbi both finished with none. It lines up with why the lane against Adele read favored the whole game: with Marshal online by around 12 minutes, the sustain and survivability tools were in play early rather than only showing up late.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Phase's loadout runs the Vesh major with The Tenth Seal and Mind Rot, which adds bonus damage whenever an ability lands on a hero and scales further the lower the target's health is, then boosts ultimate damage on top. That fits a kit that heals through its own ability casts and wants its ultimate landing hard in a group fight, rather than a pure armor-stacking pick that would trade that pressure for more durability. Against Adele's healing on the other side, the extra teamfight damage an enchanter brings is a fair trade for that durability, especially from a lane that read favored all game.

29199160-1218-49ea-9f15-0717d1726afb.build: Legion skipped the meta core's Malady and Deathstalker, both armor-shred and execute-style anti-tank tools, for Tainted Rounds' healing reduction, Nuclear Rounds' extra ability damage, and a defensive Vainglory finish that adds a flat chunk of armor and max health. Against a comp that stacked healing through Adele and hit from four different physical sources, the anti-heal and the late defensive pivot mattered as much as the missing armor shred would have. Legion finished 15 kills for 2 deaths, both late in team fights rather than in a drawn-out lane duel, so the survivability item did its job of keeping Legion alive to convert kills rather than trade them.
29199160-1218-49ea-9f15-0717d1726afb.eternal: Legion's loadout runs the same Vermis major as Yin's, with Serration and Melting Point, rewarding repeated basic attacks on one target and hitting harder against a stacked-up frontline. For a marksman carry, that is squarely the right style: the trade is giving up a burst-mage-style opening spike for damage that builds the longer a fight runs, which matches a carry who finished the game out-damaging everyone at 37,515 damage to heroes across a long game rather than off one big burst window.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Shinbi ran Megacosm and Magnify in place of the meta core's Orb Of Growth, trading early scaling utility for immediate bulk, both items add a large chunk of max health, plus Magnify's magical-armor shred and self-sustain, which suits a bruiser meant to duel and hold a front line rather than scale into a late-game core. None of the five items carried armor, though, against a lineup that was four-fifths physical; zero deaths in 33 minutes says the extra health pool and the matchup covered for it, but that gap would matter more against a comp with a real dive threat than one where the enemy jungler kept getting picked off instead.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Shinbi's loadout also runs Vesh, with The Tenth Seal and Mind Rot, the same on-hit ability-damage package, which lines up with a combo that lands several abilities per fight and an ultimate that benefits from extra ultimate damage. The trade is the mirror of Yin's: giving up the sustained on-hit anti-tank shred for damage that spikes whenever cooldowns are up, which fits a kit whose win condition is stacking Track and unloading in a grouped fight rather than grinding one extended duel.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Renna finished the entire winning core, Entropy, Wraith Leggings and Overseer, before adding Oblivion Crown for pure power and Caustica, which ignores a chunk of magical armor on top of more ability power, a penetration tool aimed at chewing through a stacked defensive target rather than adding more raw output. That fits the lane: on paper the matchup against Howitzer read as the enemy's the whole game, but Renna still finished 10 kills, 2 deaths and 28,977 damage to heroes, so the completed core plus a late anti-tank item gave Renna the range to punish fights even from behind in lane.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Renna's loadout is the same Vesh package as Phase's and Shinbi's: bonus damage whenever an ability lands on a hero, amplified further against lower-health targets, plus extra ultimate damage. Every hit in Renna's kit is an ability rather than a basic attack, so this fits cleanly with no real alternative on the table; the trade is toward damage that compounds across a full rotation rather than a single opening burst, which suits a mage whose plan is to zone a fight and chunk from range.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Howitzer Land Mine (knockback), Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Adele. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Enemy is 4/5 physical — a single armor item blunts most of their damage; itemize armor on anyone diveable.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
